text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card (27.3%, 696, 3.4%, 11.27, 3.95, 37% ≈ 0.368, 0 records returned). The cautious 'inconclusive' leaning is defensible given zero documentation. The two cited claims do support the low-complexity point. However, the headline and rationale give a thin picture of the strong statistical signal, and the next steps are generic. The summary does not contrast with the high-complexity claims or use the by-complexity breakdown, so an investigator would have to redo some analysis.","problems":["Headline 'too few returned records to judge' does not convey the strong statistical outlier signal (7.9x expected, z 3.95, 166 excess 99215 claims).","Only two example claims cited, both low-complexity; the other 23 low-complexity claims and the high-complexity contrast are not used.","Next step 'larger sample' is vague; it does not specify which claims to request, e.g. the cited low-complexity 99215 claims, or how many.","It says records came back for 0 claims, then asks for a 'larger sample', which is inconsistent since no records have been returned at all; the request should be for an initial set.","Mix of 0 and 1 condition patients is lumped together; the by-complexity gradient (18% share even at 0 conditions vs peers 2.3%) is not used.","The summary does not state that excess 99215 volume is concentrated across all complexity strata, which would strengthen the case."]}
